waves.title: Early Years Funding Rates 2026-27: What Every Council Pays
waves.keywords: early years funding rates by local authority 2026, early years funding rates 2026-27, nursery funding rate per hour, funded hours rate council, pass-through rate early years
waves.brief: The launch flagship and the seed of the Funding Rate Tracker. The SERP for 'early years funding rates by local authority 2026' is held by the Commons Library, the Early Years Alliance, council PDFs and one parent-facing fee site; no publisher answers it for the owner. Write the owner's reference: what the three English entitlement rates are for 2026-27, how a council's rate is built, and what an owner should check about their own council. Structure: the national averages and their rises; the floor and the spread; how the local formula and pass-through work; the move to termly funding and what it does to cashflow; what the averages hide (supplements, SEN inclusion funds, payment timing); a short 'check your council' list (published rate, pass-through, payment schedule, how termly adjustments are reconciled); then a clearly separate paragraph noting Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland run different systems, naming each in one line and not quoting any English rate as theirs. A table of the three age bands with average, rise and lowest published rate. Close by saying Nursery Daily is building a council-by-council tracker, in one sentence, no promise of a date. Never state a single council's rate unless it is in the anchors; never call an average 'the rate'. The politics rule applies: report NDNA's and the government's positions side by side, attributed. SOURCE ANCHORS (all pre-verified 18 Sep 2026; cite in text, do not re-derive): per NDNA (15 Dec 2025), 2026-27 national average hourly rates in England are £6.42 for 3 and 4-year-olds (up 4.95%), £8.90 for 2-year-olds (up 4.36%) and £12.04 for under-2s (up 4.28%). The lowest 3 and 4-year-old rate is £6.01, paid in 50 local authority areas, and the highest £9.23, in Camden (per the Early Years Alliance and Morton Michel summaries of the DfE figures, https://www.mortonmichel.com/news/early-years-funding-rates-announced ; attribute the Camden figure to them); the lowest 2-year-old rate is £7.66 and the lowest under-2 rate £10.34, both in Rutland. Per the DfE's 2026-27 easy explainer on gov.uk, the minimum pass-through rate (the share of funding councils must pass to providers) rises from 96% to 97%, all entitlements move to termly funding from April 2026 (13 weeks summer, 14 autumn, 11 spring), and a national adjustment of +2.94% applies to the 3 and 4-year-old rates. The National Living Wage for workers aged 21 and over rose from £12.21 to £12.71 on 1 April 2026 (gov.uk). Link: https://ndna.org.uk/early-years-funding-rates-announced/ and https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/early-years-funding-2026-to-2027/early-years-funding-rates-2026-to-2027-easy-explainer . STRUCTURAL REQUIREMENTS: the exact phrase 'early years funding rates' appears in the first paragraph; every figure names England, the year and its source in the same sentence.

waves.title: How Much Is a Nursery Worth? Multiples, Places and Prices
waves.keywords: how much is a nursery worth, nursery valuation, day nursery valuation multiple, nursery business valuation UK, price per registered place nursery
waves.brief: The 'how much is a nursery worth' SERP is held entirely by brokers and a content farm (Open a Nursery, NewOwner, Eclipse, Abacus, Owen Froebel, Morgan Cox). A neutral valuation explainer backed by market data would be the only independent one. Write it for an owner thinking about selling in the next two years and for a first-time buyer. Structure: the two ways the market prices a nursery (a multiple of adjusted EBITDA, and a sense-check per registered place), what moves the multiple (occupancy, the Ofsted outcome as a risk factor stated neutrally, staff stability, freehold versus leasehold, funded-hours mix, size, location), how buyers adjust EBITDA (owner's salary, one-off costs, rent if the owner holds the freehold), who is buying and why that matters for price, and the tax point at the end (Business Asset Disposal Relief, one paragraph, pointing to the separate selling guide). Never give our own multiple as fact: quote multiples only as ranges attributed to named brokers' published guidance, and if the draft cannot attribute a multiple, it says brokers quote a range and names the drivers instead. A table of value drivers with the direction each moves price. FAQ: is a leasehold nursery worth less, does an Ofsted grade change the price, what is a nursery worth per place. SOURCE ANCHORS (pre-verified 18 Sep 2026): Christie and Co's Day Nursery Market Review 2026 (published 8 Jul 2026) counts about 15,090 UK day nurseries offering more than 870,000 places, an average of 57.6 places per setting; in H1 2026 large groups (21 or more settings) made 61% of completed transactions, medium operators (3 to 20 settings) 23% and first-time or single-setting buyers 16%; private equity-backed operators are about 6.8% of the market; Christie Finance reported a 48.4% increase in operators and entrepreneurs seeking funding over the past 12 months. Link: https://www.christie.com/news-resources/press-releases/day-nurseries-market-review-2026/ . Business Asset Disposal Relief is 18% for disposals from 6 April 2026 (14% between 6 April 2025 and 5 April 2026), against a £1m lifetime limit (gov.uk). Broker content to link and attribute, not copy: https://newowner.co.uk/blog/how-to-sell-a-nursery-uk and https://www.abacusdaynurserysales.com/how-to-sell-a-day-nursery-business-in-the-uk/ . STRUCTURAL REQUIREMENTS: 'how much is a nursery worth' in the first paragraph; no multiple appears without a named broker beside it.

waves.keywords: how to open a nursery, how to start a nursery UK, nursery start up costs, opening a day nursery England, nursery business plan
waves.brief: The 'how to open a nursery' SERP is High Speed Training, Open a Nursery in the UK, Startups.co.uk, a lender, an accountant, a broker and a CPD farm. No trade publisher. Be the version with the real sequence and attributed numbers. Structure as the actual order of decisions: the market check (occupancy and competition in the catchment, including new school-based nurseries); premises (buy, lease or convert; planning use class and change of use; outdoor space; the lease terms that matter to a childcare operator); Ofsted registration (Early Years Register, what registration involves, realistic timescales stated as a range only if attributed); the staffing plan (ratios drive headcount, so headcount drives the business plan; manager and Level 3 requirements); the funding mix (funded hours versus private fees, and why the council's rate matters from day one); fit-out and equipment; insurance; the first-year cash position including termly funding. A step table with what each step decides and who the reader will pay (planning consultant, solicitor, fit-out, software, insurer). Cost figures only as attributed ranges from named sources; where none can be attributed, name the cost line and say what drives it. Never write as if the reader is a parent. SOURCE ANCHORS (pre-verified 18 Sep 2026): EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers (gov.uk) sets minimum ratios of 1 adult to 3 children under 2 and 1 to 5 for 2-year-olds; confirm the 3-and-over ratios against the framework PDF at https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/early-years-foundation-stage-framework--2 before quoting them. 2026-27 England average funding rates per NDNA: £6.42 (3 and 4), £8.90 (2), £12.04 (under 2). National Living Wage £12.71 from 1 April 2026 (gov.uk). Christie and Co: average UK day nursery 57.6 places. Ofsted: 6,060 providers joined the register in 2025-26. STRUCTURAL REQUIREMENTS: 'how to open a nursery' in the first paragraph; the ratio numbers appear in the staffing step with the framework linked.

waves.brief: The occupancy and margin SERP is content farms (bsness.co.uk, allbusinesswealth) and two brokers. Highly winnable with honest arithmetic. Write the owner's explainer: how occupancy is measured (registered places versus sessions sold, full-time equivalent), why it is the single biggest profit lever, how the funded-hours mix changes the margin per place, and where the costs sit. Build one worked example of a hypothetical 57-place setting, clearly labelled as illustrative arithmetic, that shows how margin moves between two occupancy levels using only the anchor figures below plus explicitly stated assumptions (write each assumption as an assumption). Do not assert a sector-average occupancy or margin in our own voice; if a named broker or survey is cited for one, attribute it and date it, otherwise say published benchmarks vary and explain why. A section on what the termly funding change does to cash, and a short 'five numbers to track monthly' list. SOURCE ANCHORS (pre-verified 18 Sep 2026): average UK day nursery 57.6 places (Christie and Co, Jul 2026). England 2026-27 average funding rates £6.42, £8.90 and £12.04 per hour for 3 and 4-year-olds, 2-year-olds and under-2s (NDNA, 15 Dec 2025). Termly funding from April 2026 with 13, 14 and 11-week terms (DfE explainer). National Living Wage £12.71 from April 2026, up from £12.21; 18 to 20 rate £10.85; apprentice £8 (gov.uk). waves.brief: gov.uk owns 'ofsted framework 2026' head-on, so this is not an explainer of the framework; it is the operator's read of what the changes cost and change in the business. The competing results are vendors and trainers (Parenta, Ovivio, Eden, a booking-software blog) and a council page. THE SAFEGUARDING RULE APPLIES IN FULL: no incident, no named setting, no named group in connection with enforcement, no case, no child. Cover only the policy and its operational and cost consequences. Structure: what changed and when (inspection frequency moving to about every four years, phased in; the revised toolkit from 1 September 2026; report cards replacing single-word judgements; more unannounced visits; enhanced checks on new providers before they open); what each means for a manager's time, training budget, documentation and insurance; what a group's head office should change (monitoring across settings, since chain-level regulation is under review); a 'what to do this term' list. SOURCE ANCHORS (pre-verified 18 Sep 2026): gov.uk, 'Safer nurseries with 3,000 more surprise Ofsted visits' (22 June 2026): 3,000 additional unannounced visits a year, a tripling on the year to April 2025; over £8 million a year to Ofsted; enhanced face-to-face interviews for new providers before they start; an independent expert panel on digital devices and CCTV in settings; a review of how nursery chains are regulated.
